papers.what_it_is: A vendor educational web page from Quantum Computing Inc explaining why light is the basis of its technology and what challenges light brings.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QCi core technology is based on using light as a versatile tool for computing, communications, measurements and random number generation.
assertions.anchor: Why is light the core of our technology?, p.1
quotes: The QCi core technology is based upon using light as a versatile tool for many tasks including computing, communications, performing measurements, and generating random numbers.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own technology.

assertions.value: The authors state that light can carry a lot of information because visible light oscillates hundreds of trillions of times per second, so slightly different frequencies can be told apart, and that electronic signals typically have only an on or off state and so carry much less information.
quotes: visible photons of light consist of oscillations that occur hundreds of trillions of times per second
electronic signals on the other hand typically only have an "on" or "off" state corresponding to two different voltages, and therefore carry much less information
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement in a vendor page without a cited source or a measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is to two-level voltage signals only; it does not address modulated electronic links.

assertions.value: The authors state that the energy of a single photon is small but still much higher than the energy of thermal vibrations at room temperature, so cooling is not required in either computers or sensors.
assertions.anchor: Low (but not too low) energy, p.1
quotes: While the energy of a single photon is small, it is still much higher than the energy of thermal vibrations at room temperature, meaning that cooling is not required in either computers or sensors.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes the basis for its own platform; no calculation or measurement is shown.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is about the energy scale of a photon. It does not say that every component of a photonic device works without cooling.

assertions.value: The authors state that superconducting computers or sensors need to be cooled substantially, and that superconducting qubits require a temperature one hundred times colder than deep space.
assertions.anchor: Low (but not too low) energy, p.1
quotes: superconducting computers or sensors for example need to be cooled substantially, to protect them.
In the case of superconducting qubits to a temperature which is one hundred times colder than deep space is required.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's statement about a competing platform, with no figure or source given.
assertions.reader_inference: No temperature is given for either side of the comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that if photons are used efficiently, the power needed to run a computer can be much, much lower than for conventional computers, and that less heat is produced in the device.
assertions.anchor: Low (but not too low) energy, p.1
quotes: if the photons are used efficiently, the power required to run the computer can be much, much lower than conventional computers
less heat will be produced in a device, making engineering easier
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes expected benefits of its own approach; no measurement is shown.
assertions.reader_inference: The claim is conditional on efficient use of photons; no power figure is given.

assertions.value: The authors state that light in their devices travels at about 1/3 to 1/2 of the speed of light in empty space, and that this is not faster than the speed of electrical signals.
quotes: about 1/3 to 1/2 of the speed of light in empty space
This isn't actually any faster than the speed at which electrical signals travel.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement without a source or measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The page itself says light does not give a signal speed advantage; its speed argument rests on heat.

assertions.value: The authors state that the limit on electronics is not signal speed but heat from switching a transistor, which moves many electrons, and that light dissipates very little energy as heat, so much faster processing is possible.
quotes: The true limitations come from switching a transistor moves a lot of electrons around and releases a lot of heat
Light not only operates at a lower energy; it also dissipates very little energy as heat, so much faster processing is possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes the expected advantage of its own approach; no measurement is shown.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives no processing rate for any QCi device.

assertions.value: The authors state that light moves naturally, so it is relatively easy to bring light particles into contact with each other, and that hard optimization problems usually need a high level of interaction, with all-to-all connectivity greatly increasing the power of hardware solvers.
quotes: the natural state of light is to be moving means that it is relatively easy to move light particles into contact with each other
hard optimization problems usually require a high level of interaction and all-to-all connectivity greatly increases the power of hardware solvers for such problems
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's rationale for its own platform; no result is shown.

assertions.value: The authors state that they believe miniaturization is key for light-based technology, that light can be guided in a material on a chip with electronics integrated on the same chip, and that some devices start on a lab bench but will eventually be compact chip-based devices.
quotes: We believe that the same ability is key for technology based on light.
we can also build chips that process light, with electronics integrated into the same chips
While some of our devices may start out on a lab bench, they will eventually end up as compact and robust chip-based devices
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor states its own roadmap and belief.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a forward-looking statement, not a delivered product.

assertions.value: The authors state that their current platform is lithium niobater (as printed in the text), chosen because it provides the best optical and optoelectronic properties combined while staying compatible with chip manufacturing processes.
quotes: Our current platform is lithium niobater because it provides the best optical and optoelectronic properties combined while still being compatible with chip manufacturing processes.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the company's own platform choice (setup); the claim that it gives the best properties is a vendor claim and is not graded here.
assertions.reader_inference: The text prints the material name as lithium niobater, which is read as a misspelling of lithium niobate.

assertions.value: The authors state that light is fundamentally quantum mechanical, that non-linear optics is the key to unlocking these quantum effects, and that the individual-photon nature of light only matters for specific kinds of light.
quotes: light is fundamentally quantum mechanical and non-linear optics is the key to unlocking these quantum effects
this fact only becomes important for specific kinds of light
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement without a derivation or source on the page.

assertions.value: The authors state that the biggest challenge in working with light is getting photons to interact, that non-interaction is an advantage for communication (different frequencies share one fiber independently), and that it is a challenge for computing and processing.
assertions.anchor: Challenges of working with light, p.1
quotes: The biggest challenge is getting photons to interact.
different frequencies can be used to send multiple streams of information through the same optical fiber in a way that is mutually independent of each other

the lack of interactions between light particles which allows large quantities of information to be transmitted through a fiber-optic cable presents a challenge when the light is used instead to compute or otherwise process information
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement in a vendor page; it is also a stated limit of the approach, but the page gives no derivation.

assertions.value: The authors state that interactions between light particles are also needed to make interesting quantum states of light.
assertions.anchor: Challenges of working with light, p.1
quotes: interactions of some kind between light particles are also needed to make interesting quantum states of light
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement without a derivation on the page.

assertions.value: The authors state that a single simple logic gate, a NAND gate, which outputs a low voltage if and only if both inputs are high, can be used to build arbitrarily complex logic, and that this illustrates that a large range of photon interactions is not needed, only a few operations done extremely well.
assertions.anchor: Challenges of working with light, p.1
quotes: a single very simple logic gate, one which outputs a low voltage if and only if both inputs are a high voltage, and a high voltage otherwise (a NAND gate) can be used to build arbitrarily complex logic
what we need is to do a few things extremely well and use these operations together for a multitude of applications
assertions.certainty_reason: A standard fact stated without a source or proof on the page, used here as an analogy for photonic operations.
assertions.reader_inference: The NAND result is a standard classical-logic fact. The page gives no photonic equivalent.

assertions.value: The authors state that they target a multitude of platforms for their optical technology because the underlying challenges in manipulating particles of light are the same, and that their fabrication of on-chip quantum optic devices will allow key components to be used in a versatile way.
assertions.anchor: Challenges of working with light, p.1
quotes: we are targeting a multitude of platforms for our optical technology: the underlying challenges in manipulating particles of light are the same
extremely high-quality fabrication of on-chip quantum optic devices will allow us to develop key components which will be used in a versatile way
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own strategy.

assertions.value: The authors state that by manipulating light precisely, eventually at the single particle level, they will be able to build devices not currently possible, including devices that harness quantum superposition and interference to compute.
assertions.anchor: Challenges of working with light, p.1
quotes: By being able to precisely manipulate the behavior of light, eventually, at the single particle level, we will be able to build devices that are currently not possible
including devices that can harness quantum superposition and interference to compute
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor states a future goal for its own technology; no result is shown.
assertions.reader_inference: The word eventually marks this as a goal, not a present capability.

assertions.value: The authors state that the cited quantum-gate work shows how their core technology can manipulate single photons in a quantum way, while quantum gates are not their current approach to computing.
quotes: build quantum gates, which while not our current approach to computing does demonstrate how it can be used to manipulate photons single photons in a quantum way
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the scope of the company's own computing approach (gate-based quantum computing is not the current approach).
assertions.reader_inference: The page links DOI 10.1109/JSTQE.2011.2116111 for this work and does not describe its results.

assertions.value: The authors state that the first linked work in the Further reading list shows their core technology can make a very effective source of single light particles, needed in a large number of quantum optics applications.
quotes: This work demonstrates how our core technology can be used to make a very effective source of single light particles, which are needed in a large number of quantum optics applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result that the page summarizes in one sentence; the paper itself is not read here.
assertions.reader_inference: The link between the sentence and the DOI is by order on the page; the DOI text is in the page's link list.

assertions.value: The authors state that the third linked work in the Further reading list shows how light can be manipulated on a chip and how different beams of light can be made to interact effectively.
quotes: This work demonstrates how we can manipulate light on a chip, and effectively interact different beams of light.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result that the page summarizes in one sentence; the paper itself is not read here.

assertions.value: The authors state that they have patented key technology to overcome the limitations in photon interactions, and name patent US11754908B2 for it.
quotes: We have patented key technology to overcome the limitations in photon interactions, allowing us to overcome a key bottleneck.
https://patents.google.com/patent/US11754908B2/en
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own patent; that the patent overcomes the bottleneck is a vendor claim.
assertions.reader_inference: A patent grant is not evidence that the limitation is overcome in a working device.

assertions.value: The authors state that the page is a high-level overview and that deeper research is linked, with no experimental results, measurements or proofs given on the page itself.
quotes: This page is a high-level overview.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states its own scope.
assertions.reader_inference: The second half of the value (no results on the page) is the reader's observation from reading the whole page.
